plan.title: Hallmark ssGSEA scoring: CD inflamed vs control ileum
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question is per-sample hallmark signature scores plus a between-group test on those scores, for 12 human ileal bulk RNA-seq samples (6 Crohn disease inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes x 12 samples of Salmon gene-level counts). Two data facts drive the design. First, sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median — single-sample gene-set scoring methods are sensitive to library depth and to the resulting inflated dropout, so the pipeline must normalize on a depth-robust basis and must explicitly check whether sample_01's scores are outliers before any biological reading. Second, only 12,000 genes are present (a pre-filtered matrix, not a full transcriptome), so hallmark set coverage will be incomplete and must be quantified per set — a hallmark with few detected members gives an unstable score and should be flagged rather than reported alongside well-covered sets.

T1S1 prepares the expression matrix: filter low-count genes on a CPM basis (not raw counts, which would penalize sample_01 twice), normalize with a between-sample method robust to depth (DESeq2 size factors / VST, or TMM-logCPM), map row identifiers to HGNC symbols since the hallmark GMT is symbol-keyed, resolve duplicate symbols, and quantify sample_01's depth effect (library sizes, per-sample detected-gene counts, sample-sample correlation, PCA) so the caveat is measured rather than assumed. T1S2 computes the actual answer: a 50 x 12 hallmark score matrix by ssGSEA/GSVA on the normalized matrix, with singscore as an independent rank-based cross-check, plus per-set coverage. T1S3 tests each hallmark score for a difference between inflamed and control with limma on the score matrix (moderated t, BH across the 50 sets), reports effect sizes and CIs, and repeats the test with sample_01 dropped as a leave-one-out sensitivity check — with n=6 per group a single influential sample can create or destroy a hit. T2S1 runs a gene-level differential expression and a hallmark GSEA on the DESeq2-ranked gene list as an orthogonal route to the same conclusion; a hallmark that moves in the score test but not in the ranked GSEA is a scoring artifact, not biology. It runs in parallel from T1S1 and its result is compared in T1S3's reporting? No — the concordance comparison lives in T2S1 itself, which depends on both T1S2 and T1S3, keeping the DAG acyclic.
